subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` boolean, and what safety semantics should it use for failed mutating tools after success-looking replies?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but choosing whether to hide or defer failed mutating-tool warnings changes public config and user-visible safety behavior.

options.title: Approve default-compatible policy
options.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after regression coverage proves real failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

options.title: Keep the boolean opt-out
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported operator escape hatch and close or narrow the final-only request to docs and channel-specific leaks.

options.title: Split narrow leaks first
options.body: Defer the enum and address remaining Feishu, exec-like, lifecycle, or channel-specific warning leaks as separate issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible policy
recommendation.body: Add a documented `all` default with explicit `final` and/or `off` modes only after regression coverage proves real failed mutations are not silently confirmed.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged warning-policy PR explicitly scoped this issue as the remaining broader policy/config decision.
